messages.subject: assembly argument when creating myobj
parts:
Hi
I'm reading four files (duplicates for genotype C and duplicates for genotype B), see below.

> comparisonName="C_ctrl_vs_B_ctrol_unite_filter_compare";
> chrom="chr1";
> B4_ctrl="BC2"; B7_ctrl="BC6";
> C4_ctrl="BC1"; C7_ctrl="BC5";
> B1=paste(B4_ctrl, chrom, "MethylKit.inputdata.CpG.txt", sep=".");
> B2=paste(B7_ctrl, chrom, "MethylKit.inputdata.CpG.txt", sep=".");
> C1=paste(C4_ctrl, chrom, "MethylKit.inputdata.CpG.txt", sep=".");
> C2=paste(C7_ctrl, chrom, "MethylKit.inputdata.CpG.txt", sep=".");
> file.list <- list(B1,B2,C1,C2);

> myobj <- read(file.list, sample.id = list(B1,B2,C1,C2), assembly="TAIR10", treatment=c(1,1,0,0), context="CpG");

I put TAIR10 as a value for the assembly argument, but I have not file in my working directory that represents TAIR10.
The point is that the files were read and not warning message appear. So my question are:
1) do I need to have a file called TAIR10 in my working directory?
2) at this point of the analysis, this file need to be the genome or the 12column BED annotation file?
3) what happens if I keep working without such a file? Are there thinks that I can not do later?
I will appreciate the help
Ale

messages.author: e4181d5c40fc094c
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] assembly argument when creating myobj
parts:
You have read it what it means. A 'string' is a 'character' it doesn't need to be a file. A 'string' is stored as such!

methylKit don't need a file. Infact, by assigning 'TAIR10' you are simply telling it that you have aligned your data with a genome named 'TAIR10'. At no point methylkit require the actual 'TAIR10' genome.

It is worth to go through the definition of terms in R!

Regards,
Kalyan

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] assembly argument when creating myobj
parts:
Kalyan is right about the assembly argument, it is just a string so that users know what assembly is used in alignment process at any given time. AFAIR, It will also prohibit users using objects that have different assemblies in certain functions.

12 column BED file is needed for annotation (refer to vignette on how and where to use it) you don't need it if you don't need to annotate your DMRs/DMCs. Again, clear examples are all around on how that works: paper, vignette, this forum. Also search for TAIR10 in the forum, there were other people trying to use that assembly.
